algorithm_frozen.separate: each statistic is ranked on its own against each reference set: 2 statistics x 2 reference sets = 4 results; no combined rank, no combined direction

algorithm_frozen.reference_median: numpy.median of the reference specimens' values (the target is never part of its own reference set; a reference specimen without a value is dropped and listed as unranked)
algorithm_frozen.ranked_population: the reference specimens with a value plus the target
algorithm_frozen.direction: above | below | equal, from value - reference median; equal iff |value - reference median| <= 1e-12
algorithm_frozen.rank: 1 + number of ranked specimens whose deviation exceeds the target's deviation by more than 1e-12 (competition ranking; rank 1 = largest deviation)
algorithm_frozen.ties: deviations within the tolerance share the LOWER rank number; the target exactly at the reference median has deviation 0, direction 'equal', and ties only with other zero-deviation specimens (with an odd reference set the median is a reference specimen's own value, so at least one tie); no jitter or secondary key
algorithm_frozen.no_value: a specimen with no eligible compartment or non-finite values has no statistic: it is not ranked and is listed; a target without a value has rank null and typed not_estimable

H4.inference: none: rank only, no p-value, no interval

models.magnitude: linear model: log(sender score among actives) ~ group + covariates + block fixed effects
models.participation: logistic regression: active ~ group + covariates (no block fixed effects; separation risk; blocks enter through the bootstrap resampling)
models.covariate_note: log(n_st_eff) removed (A12.3 fix round). With n_st measured with noise, adding log(n_st_eff) to the covariates produces a group-effect bias in the synthetic noisy-n_st null that grows with the noise: mean plain-OLS group t among actives with vs without it, at sigma_n 0.01 / 0.4 / 0.8, is in synthetic/g6_fix/diag_collider_noise_dose.json (with: 0.05 / 0.69 / 0.75; without: -0.14 / -0.15 / -0.15) (script src/diag_collider_noise_dose.py, 300 datasets). A collider-type path (log E_o is recoverable from log(n_st_eff), log(spot_umi) and log(rna_per_cell_equiv), and the keratin share's denominator contains E_o) is consistent with this dose-response, but the exact causal path is NOT demonstrated. Trade-off: on real data n_st (StarDist counts) is noisy, so dropping it avoids the label bias, but the outcome still depends on the true cell number, and the remaining adjustment rests on log(rna_per_cell_equiv) and depth only. Magnitude blocks: 6-pitch tiles
models.covariate_domain_rule: Frozen (replaces any floor): log(spot_umi) and log(rna_per_cell_equiv) require every value finite and strictly > 0; qp_prop must be finite. Otherwise typed not_estimable (covariate_domain). No value is ever floored or replaced.
models.standardisation: the three covariates are standardised ONCE over the specimen's eligible cancer compartments (all rows of the run, population SD ddof=0), never per bootstrap resample, per label shift or per subset. Covariates are the same for R00, R01, R02, R10; R11 swaps rna_per_cell_equiv for rna_per_cell_equiv_nf only.
models.log_n_st_eff: not a covariate; available only by explicit opt-in (include_log_n_st_eff=True) for sensitivity work, never in a protocol run

bootstrap.min_valid_fraction_justification: a PRESPECIFIED QC CONVENTION, not a coverage guarantee and not empirically tuned. Each tail of the 95% interval holds 2.5% of the resamples (5% in total); if more than 5% of the 2000 resamples are invalid the retained resamples cannot be treated as the full bootstrap distribution at the tail quantiles. >= 0.95 of 2000 = at least 1900 valid resamples. Invalid resamples may be non-random (they are the resamples that lose a group or a block), so passing the threshold does NOT imply that the nominal level is preserved; the measured coverage (0.874-0.900 historical, 0.884-0.904 production path, in which every resample was valid) is the only evidence about the level. The earlier code used > 0.5, which is not frozen here
bootstrap.valid_resample: a resample is valid iff both groups keep positive weight among active senders, the weighted design is full rank (smallest/largest eigenvalue of X'WX > 1e-10) and the group coefficient is finite
bootstrap.interval_policy: NOMINAL 95% interval, never widened or inflated. It is reported with its measured synthetic coverage (0.874, 0.896, 0.898, 0.900; all four null cases, from synthetic/g6_fix/boot_*_s6.json) and the valid-resample fraction. Wording never depends on whether the interval excludes 1.

genotype_groups.k0_justification: Convention fixed without real data: keratin-high if k_share >= 0.01, i.e. the six basal keratins make up at least 1% of the compartment's partitioned counts. A share is free of n_st (removes the shared denominator that let n_st noise leak into the label), and 0.01 is a round fraction not tuned on any outcome. Honest note: 0.01 is NOT independent of the synthetic generator. It equals the generator's baseline keratin share (E_k mean 2 vs E_o mean 200, 2/202 = 0.0099), and the sensitivity grid (0.005, 0.02) was chosen around it. It is therefore a pre-set convention, not evidence about real keratin biology, and its prevalence on real data is unknown. The synthetic G6 gate used its own generator-specific threshold (0.0143791, pooled 0.70 quantile of the generator's k_share, seeds 900000-900019) only to give 30% prevalence; it does not transfer to real data.

k0_fallback.trigger: ONLY if either group (high or low) has fewer than 30 eligible compartments at k0 = 0.01 in that specimen. The decision uses the compartment counts and k_share alone, is taken before COMMOT runs and before any outcome exists. The active-sender count is NOT a trigger.
k0_fallback.fallback: within-specimen threshold = numpy.quantile(k_share over the specimen's eligible cancer compartments, 0.70, method='linear'); high = k_share >= that quantile (ties go to HIGH). Applied once.
k0_fallback.after_selection: once a threshold is chosen, the active-sender gate (>= 10 per group, magnitude) and the mixed-block gate (>= 10 mixed blocks) are applied as ordinary typed gates with NO further fallback and no other threshold
k0_fallback.reporting: state per specimen which rule was used (absolute_k0_0.01 or fallback_quantile_0.70); if either group is still < 30 under the fallback the specimen is not_estimable (group_size)

algorithm_frozen.sensitivity_labels: A03/A04 use the absolute rule with the group-size gate and no fallback; A05-A07 as listed under sensitivity

genotype_groups.label_variable: k_share = sum over the six genes (KRT5, KRT6A, KRT6B, KRT14, KRT16, KRT17) of E_stg / ( sum over all genes of E_stg MINUS E_st,MDK ): the compartment's keratin share of its own allocated counts EXCLUDING the tested outcome MDK. Linear counts only: neither n_st nor depth_ratio enters it, and MDK (the outcome) cannot set its own label; a fold-3 MDK injection therefore cannot change membership. Implemented in src/compartments.py (obs column k_share). The per-cell-equivalent form E/n_st_eff/depth_ratio is a descriptive column only (k_percell_desc).
genotype_groups.label_rule: keratin-high iff k_share >= k0 (the boundary value is HIGH)
genotype_groups.synthetic_generator_note: src/synthetic_g6.py builds the same label: k_share = E_k / max(E_o + E_k, 1) with E_o = the non-keratin, non-MDK counts, so the synthetic label excludes MDK as well (verified; mutation kshare_label_depends_on_n_st).
genotype_groups.historical_label_k_st: HISTORICAL (withdrawn): revisions 1-5 of the spec used the per-cell label k_st = sum E/n_st_eff/depth_ratio >= 1.0 (sensitivities 0.25, 2.0). It is HISTORICAL: it let the nuclei estimate and depth enter the label and was replaced by k_share in revision 5; revision 6 removes the remaining k_st uses.
